whatItIs.text: Tunisia's hot chilli paste — roasted red and Baklouti peppers with garlic, caraway, coriander, cumin, and olive oil carrying the flavour.

historyNote.text: Chillies reached Tunisia with the Columbian exchange, presumably during the Spanish occupation of 1535-1574, and harissa grew up on the Cape Bon Peninsula; UNESCO inscribed the paste and its traditions as Intangible Cultural Heritage in 2022.

howToChoose.text: Rose harissa adds floral softness, classic versions more fire; check that peppers, not fillers, lead the ingredient list, and start with less than you think.

storage.text: Refrigerate after opening with a film of oil on top. The rulebook has the window.
storage.note: opened-jar guidance lives in the food-safety rulebook

useItUp.text: Stir it into soups, stews, and couscous, or thin with oil and lemon for a grill marinade; a dab lifts eggs, yoghurt, and roast vegetables.

substitutions.note: builds the same warmth without the paste body
